blurb: Cat-like Japanese toy spaniel bred as a companion for royalty and nobility
description: The Japanese Chin is a small toy companion dog from Japan with a broad round head, large dark eyes and a silky single coat, described as charming and cat-like.
answer: The Japanese Chin, also known as the Japanese Spaniel, is a toy lap and companion dog from Japan with a long aristocratic history. It stands about 25 cm at the withers and is known for its broad round head, short muzzle, silky single coat and cat-like manner.

body: Most accounts hold that the Chin's ancestors came from China, but how they reached Japan is debated. One story says the dogs were given to the Japanese court in AD 732 by an envoy from the Korean kingdom of Silla; others date their arrival to the sixth or seventh century, or to around AD 1000. A Chin was brought to England in 1613, and US naval officer Matthew Perry acquired one in 1853. Since 1868 the breed has been kept as a lapdog by upper-class ladies and today is a companion dog.

The Chin has a large, rounded, broad head, large wide-set dark eyes, a very short broad muzzle, feathered ears and evenly patterned facial markings. Unlike most dogs it has only an outer coat, with no undercoat, and the adult coat can take up to two years to grow in. Colours are black and white, red and white (including sable, lemon and orange shades), or tricolour. The FCI sets no weight requirement.

The breed is commonly described as cat-like, charming, fun and entertaining, but also stubborn and temperamental. Chins can show signs of separation anxiety, which sources say crate training can help address.

Japanese Chins enjoy walks and are described as moderately active, yet suitable for smaller homes such as flats. Because they can be stubborn, sources recommend not letting them off the leash outdoors.

One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years, close to the 12.7-year average for purebreds. Conditions reported in the breed include luxating patellas, cataracts and early-onset heart murmurs.

faq.q: How long do Japanese Chins live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years.

faq.q: Are Japanese Chins good apartment dogs?
faq.a: They are described as moderately active dogs that enjoy walks but adapt well to small living spaces such as flats.

faq.q: Is the Japanese Chin recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 206 in Group 9, with Japan as the country of origin.
